title: The test rules say a change gets no test by default and only a critical component keeps one
goal: kb/_self/code.md "Checks and their tests" says "A change gets no test by default" and "A test exists only for a critical component", naming the critical kinds (secret, leak and untrusted-code guards; the push and publish gates, the query log never reaching the public home included; operator-only authority: the gate classes, the ceiling class and the agent-session guard; formats another tool parses); it says a bug is proven by its repro and user feedback, not a test, and that a planner prefers deleting or merging tests to speeding them up, while its ceiling rules stay (an agent never raises it, a ceiling gate is the operator's own); the matching lines of kb/_self/backlog.md, kb/_self/maintaining.md, skills/sprint/SKILL.md plan steps 2 and 6 and review step 4, skills/item/SKILL.md step 6, skills/backlog/SKILL.md bug step 1 and agents/worker.md say the same and drop the land e2e test reason; the _self eval rows that pinned the old wording follow, so rag.py eval --root _self passes. Code-lane paths (skills/, agents/, the eval file): done and the push to main come after its merge request merges (backlog.py land ID --wait-merge 1800).

gates.question: What does the project test, now that the operator has stated its test policy (2026-10-16)?
